bio_am: Շանայէն։ 18 Յուլիս 1921-ին Պոլսոյ մէջ ահաբեկեց Պէհպուտ Խան Ճիւանշիրը, անգլիական ատեանը զինք անպարտ արձակեց։
bio_en: Misak Torlakian, a native of Shana, belonged to the small band of avengers of 1921-22, alongside Tehlirian, Yerkanian and Shirakian. After Abraham Gyulkhandanian recognised Behbud Khan Javanshir, the former Azerbaijani interior minister held responsible for the massacre of Armenians in Baku, in Constantinople, Torlakian was assigned with Yervand Fndkian and Harutiun Harutiunian to track him. On 18 July 1921 in Pera, as crowds left the Petits-Champs theatre, he shot Javanshir outside the Pera Palace hotel and was seized on the spot. Tried for two months before a British court-martial in Constantinople, he was acquitted, the verdict being announced in late 1921. He later wrote the memoir 'With my days', prefaced by Malkhas, and died in November 1968.
notes: Compiled from the archive review, 2026-10-12. Confidence: high. #547 gives the date of the killing as 15 March; #559 and #666 give 18 July 1921 (used).
